title: A probe that cannot read RAM fails open in silence
body:
## Summary
When the probe cannot read RAM or CPU the gate fails open, as designed, but nothing is logged, so a PC whose memory reader broke admits every task with no trace.

## Description
src/athena/vitals/probe.py:502 `_safe` swallows every reader exception into `None`; src/athena/vitals/gate.py:381 `_held` treats `ram_pct is None` as open; src/athena/vitals/sampler.py:79 logs only an exception that escapes `sample()`, which a None never is. The registry technique admission-queue/load-aware-admission ('The probe is a component, and it can lie': 'Fail-open with a logged warning is usually right ... the choice is ... stated in the gate') asks for the warning. Fixed looks like: one stderr line (or a ledger/bus event) when a figure the gate needs turns unknown, one when it comes back - transitions, not every 5 s.

## Flow
- a reader raises (e.g. GlobalMemoryStatusEx fails) -> `_safe` returns None -> Reading.ram_pct None
- Gate.observe -> held() None, room null -> tasks start, nothing in stderr or on the bus beyond room: null
- operator asking 'why did three tasks start on a full PC' finds no line

## Expected impact
An operator diagnosing a misbehaving PC; measured by stderr lines on a scripted None run. Could break: log noise if the transition logic flaps.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - an unknown figure is said once when it turns unknown
Before: 0 lines logged across 10 readings with memory reader raising (read from code: no logging path)
After: 1 line at the turn to unknown, 1 at recovery (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked the three call sites; the instrument (a capsys test over Gate/Sampler with a raising reader) is S but where the line goes (stderr vs bus vs ledger) is a design pick
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/vitals/probe.py:502-507 _safe -> None
src/athena/vitals/gate.py:381 `if self._ram_held and reading.ram_pct is not None`
src/athena/vitals/sampler.py:79-81 only an escaped exception prints
instrument: capsys test: Probe with a raising memory reader sampled 10x through Sampler.sample -> count stderr lines; Before 0, After 2 (turn unknown, recover)

title: A sampler that keeps failing prints every 5 s and never says why
body:
## Summary
A reading that raises prints '[vitals] a reading raised <Type>' every 5 s for as long as it raises, without the message, so a persistent fault is 17,280 identical lines a day that do not name it.

## Description
src/athena/vitals/sampler.py:79-81 prints `type(exc).__name__` only, on every tick (`every_s` = 5 s, src/athena/vitals/__init__.py:56). The sleep loop beside it prints type and message (src/athena/daemon/sleep.py:304-307), so the two hosted loops disagree. Fixed: print the first failure with its message, then only when the failure changes or clears.

## Flow
- gate.observe raises (e.g. a provider bug outside _guarded) -> Sampler._run catches -> prints type -> waits 5 s -> repeats
- stderr fills with one line per 5 s; the message that would name the bug is never printed

## Expected impact
Whoever reads the daemon log; measured by lines per hour under a persistent fault. Could break: a real second failure hidden if dedup keys too coarsely.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a persistent fault is said once, with its message
Before: 720 lines/hour, 0 with a message (computed from every_s=5 and the print at sampler.py:81)
After: 1 line with the message, plus 1 when it clears (predicted)
Method: simulation - computed from the loop period; a capsys test with a raising gate over N ticks of a fast every_s would decide it
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/vitals/sampler.py:77-83
    except Exception as exc:  # a reading's bug must not end the loop
        with suppress(Exception):
            print(f"[vitals] a reading raised {type(exc).__name__}", file=sys.stderr)
instrument: capsys test: Sampler(every_s=0.01) over a gate whose observe raises, run 20 ticks -> count lines and check the message is present; Before 20/0, After 1/1

title: This PC's gate trusts its latest reading at any age
body:
## Summary
The local gate (and so the sleep admission's RAM hold and every task claim) reads the sampler's latest reading with no age check; ADR 0143's 90 s staleness rule applies only to peers.

## Description
src/athena/vitals/gate.py:377-407 `_held` and :440 `task_room` use `self._reading` whatever its `at`; `VITALS_STALE_S` (src/athena/vitals/__init__.py:77) is applied to peers only (ADR 0143 'The fleet': 'a stale "room ok" is worse than none'). If the sampler stops or blocks (it is stopped by `VitalsService.stop`, and `Probe.read` holds a lock across a 3 s subprocess), a frozen 'RAM 95%' holds sleep forever and a frozen 'ok' admits work on a PC that has since filled. Fixed looks like: a reading older than N x SAMPLE_EVERY_S reads as unknown. That makes a stale hold fail OPEN, which loosens a hold: a policy call for the owner, and an ADR amendment.

## Flow
- sampler stops (shutdown race) or a reader blocks -> gate keeps the last Reading
- admission asks held(sleep=True) -> answers from a reading of any age

## Expected impact
The person whose PC fills while the sampler is wedged; measured by a gate with an injected clock. Could break: a slow but healthy sampler reading as unknown.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the gate never acts on a reading older than its staleness line
Before: a reading 10 min old still decides held() (read from code)
After: a reading older than 3 samples reads as unknown (proposed)
Method: simulation - walked _held/task_room; the instrument is a Gate with a clock test, S, but the rule is an owner decision
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-loosen
evidence:
src/athena/vitals/gate.py:377-380 `reading = self._reading; if reading is None: return None` - no age check
src/athena/vitals/__init__.py:76-77 VITALS_STALE_S documented for peers only

title: Forget bars and the degraded merge scan every live memory per call
body:
## Summary
`SleepBook.bars()` reads every live fact and procedural of a space's view once per partition, and the degraded merge's `same_key()` reads them all again once per candidate (up to 18), comparing keys in Python.

## Description
src/athena/core/sleep/book.py:668-679 selects every live memory (`WHERE {_LIVE} AND {_wall(seen)}`) to find keys written after a marker; src/athena/core/sleep/book.py:697-706 does a full scan per candidate and normalizes in Python because `norm_key` (casefold + whitespace) has no SQL index. Called from src/athena/core/sleep/cycle.py:387 per partition and cycle.py:408 per candidate. On a brain with tens of thousands of memories that is up to 19 full scans per partition inside one cycle. Fixed looks like: restrict the second query in bars() to the marked keys (an IN over the barred (kind, scope) rows), and build one norm_key -> row map per partition for same_key.

## Flow
- a cycle with 12 facts + 6 procedurals whose merge leg fails -> _by_key -> 18 x same_key -> 18 full scans
- bars() once per partition -> 1 more full scan each

## Expected impact
Sleep cycle wall time on a large brain; measured by timing bars()+same_key over a brain seeded with 5,000 facts. Could break: a bar or duplicate missed if the narrowed query drops a case-folded key.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one scan per partition instead of up to 19
Before: 19 full scans of live memories per partition in the degraded path (counted from code)
After: 1 scan per partition (proposed); timing not taken
Method: simulation - counted call sites; timing needs a seeded brain harness (S) the round did not build
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/core/sleep/book.py:668-679, 697-706
src/athena/core/sleep/cycle.py:387 bars(space); :408 same_key per candidate
instrument: pytest timing harness: Brain with 5,000 facts + 3 forget markers; time cycle._by_key(18 candidates) and book.bars(); Before/After ms, plus the existing bars/same_key tests green

title: A failed cycle stamped ahead of the clock reads 'failed 1 min ago'
body:
## Summary
The failed_recently sentence has the same clamp the floor sentence had: a failed row stamped in this computer's future reads 'The last cycle failed 1 min ago' while the backoff holds for hours more.

## Description
src/athena/core/sleep/admission.py (failed_recently branch) formats `_ago(failed_since)`; `_ago` clamps a negative figure to '1 min'. The floor branch was fixed this round (4537fdf2) to say the stamp is ahead of the clock; this branch was left. Fixed: the same wording for the failure sentence, both the one-failure and the N-in-a-row forms.

## Flow
- clock set back after a failed cycle -> failed_since < 0 -> verdict text 'failed 1 min ago; trying again after 1 h'

## Expected impact
The person reading Mind > Brain's sleep verdict. Could break: nothing beyond the sentence; the hold is unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the failure sentence states the stamp honestly
Before: 'The last cycle failed 1 min ago; trying again after 1 h.' for a row stamped 3 h ahead (same mechanism as the floor, red-tested this round)
After: 'The last cycle is stamped 3 h ahead of this computer's clock; trying again after 1 h.' (predicted)
Method: simulation - same code shape as the floor fix, whose test went red-then-green; not built to keep the round's commit to one finding
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/core/sleep/admission.py failed_recently branch: f"The last cycle failed {_ago(failed_since)} ago; ..."
src/athena/core/sleep/admission.py _ago: `max(1, int(hours * 60))`
instrument: copy test_a_cycle_stamped_ahead_of_the_clock_still_holds_and_says_so with a failed row (_failed_row hours_ago=-3) asserting the new sentence
